findings.detail: In `/^[+-]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(e[+-]?\d+)?$/i`, the branch `\d+\.?\d*` is ambiguous: because `\.?` can match empty, a run of digits can be split between `\d+` and `\d*` in N different ways. On input that is a long digit run followed by a character that fails the anchor (e.g. a 30,000-character numeric-looking cell ending in a stray letter — Excel permits 32,767 chars per cell), the engine explores O(N^2) splits before returning `false`, on the main thread, once per quantity cell. This is not exponential and needs a pathological cell to be noticeable, so it is not a realistic user-facing freeze today; what would raise it to medium is any path that feeds this function untrimmed multi-KB text routinely. The fix is free and does not change which strings are accepted.
findings.summary: Ambiguous `\d+\.?\d*` alternative backtracks quadratically on a long non-matching cell

findings.detail: The audit is accurate and well-evidenced — I verified defect #1 (`runLookup` line 165 keeps the first row for a duplicate key, `handleDownload` line 221 keeps the last) and defect #3 (`if (!ws[ref].s)` dereferences `ws[ref]` before checking it exists, line 275) directly against the source. Defect #1 is a P0 that ships a file differing from the approved preview. The document is explicit that it is an audit record and that nothing is fixed yet, which is the right call for a no-code-change PR. The only gap is ownership: the P0 items carry a priority but no issue number or owner, so the "recorded" half of deliberate-recorded-owned is satisfied and the "owned" half is not. Purely advisory — this does not affect the verdict.
findings.summary: Four confirmed defects recorded with priorities but no tracking references
